GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/dateForma.summary: Lists the date/time display styles the plugin can use when rendering date values in columns and exports, each with a sample rendering of the current moment in the caller's locale and time zone. Read-only.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/dateForma.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.summary: Returns the Jira create-screen editor HTML for fields, so the client can show inline issue creation. The prospective issue is defined either by a sample issue (its project, issue type and, for sub-tasks, parent are reused, and copyable field values are pre-filled from it) or by an explicit project and issue type; other fields get Jira's defaults. Project, summary and (unless a sub-task) issue type are skipped when field values are filled in, but are rendered like any other field if requested and on the screen. Special case: when no sample is given and `field` lists exactly `project` and `issuetype`, only the project and issue-type pickers are rendered and the reply lists the projects where the caller may create issues and the plugin is enabled. Nothing is created or changed. A field the caller cannot use is still listed but carries a per-field `error` text instead of HTML (field hidden for this issue, made read-only by a third-party scripting app, or rendering failed); requested field ids that are not on the relevant screen get an entry with only an `error`.

params.sample: Issue id (numeric) of a sample issue. Optional. If the issue does not exist or the caller cannot browse it, the reply is 200 with a top-level `error` and no fields.
params.project: Project id (numeric). Required together with `issuetype` unless `sample` is given; overrides the sample's project.
params.issuetype: Issue type id (string). Required together with `project` unless `sample` is given; overrides the sample's type.
params.field: Repeatable; Jira field ids to render (e.g. `assignee`, `customfield_10010`, `status`). Omitted or empty: every field on the create screen except issue links, time logged and attachments.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestIssueFields}} where `forCreate` is true and `fields` holds `createHtml` per field id.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.errors: 400 (plain text) when neither a sample nor both project and issue type are given, when the project id is rejected by Jira, or when the issue type does not exist. 403 (plain text `permission violation`) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.summary: Returns the inline-edit HTML for one field of a plugin-native item (only memos and planning tasks support fields). The item is identified by its short type name and numeric id; the item type id is formed by prefixing the plugin key, e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo`. Read-only.

params.type: Short item type name: `memo` or `planning-task`. Required; any other value gives 400.
params.id: Numeric item id. If omitted, 0 is used (no such item, so the reply carries an `error`).
params.field: Id of the plugin-level item field to edit (e.g. a summary/description-like field of the memo). Required.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestItemFields}}. When the item does not exist, the field is unknown or not visible for that item type, or the field is not editable, the reply has a top-level `error` and no `fields`; when rendering fails the single field entry carries an `error`.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.errors: 400 (plain text) when `type` or `field` is missing or the type does not support fields. 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.summary: Shortcut for the generic-item variant with the item type fixed to memo: returns the inline-edit HTML for one field of a memo.

params.memoId: Numeric memo id. Required in practice: when omitted the call fails with a server error (500).
params.fieldId: Id of the memo field to edit. Required (400 when missing).

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestItemFields}}, same rules as the generic-item variant.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.errors: 400 (plain text) when `fieldId` is missing; 500 when `memoId` is missing; 403 (plain text) without the plugin's 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.summary: Returns Jira edit-screen editor HTML for fields of an existing issue, current values pre-filled, so the client can edit cells inline. If `status` is among the requested fields, a status editor is rendered that offers the workflow transitions the caller can execute on the issue. Also reports whether the original estimate may be changed (false when time is already logged and Jira's legacy time-tracking mode is on). Read-only. A field the caller cannot use is still listed but carries a per-field `error` text instead of HTML (field hidden for this issue, made read-only by a third-party scripting app, or rendering failed); requested field ids that are not on the relevant screen get an entry with only an `error`.

params.issue: Issue id (numeric). Required. Unknown or not browsable by the caller: 200 with a top-level `error`.
params.field: Repeatable; Jira field ids to render. Omitted or empty: all edit-screen fields except issue links, time logged and attachments.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestIssueFields}} where `fields` holds `editHtml` per field id.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/fields/fo.errors: 400 (plain text) when `issue` is missing; 403 (plain text) without the plugin's 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/groups.summary: Lists Jira user groups by name. With `assignable=true` it returns the groups the caller may use in plugin permission rules: the caller's own groups, or all groups when the caller is a Jira administrator or the instance property `structure.permissions.allowAllUserGroups` is on; anonymous callers get an empty list. Without it, all groups are returned, which requires Jira administrator or the global 'browse users' permission.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/groups.errors: 403 (plain text) when listing all groups without administrator or 'browse users' permission; 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/license.summary: Returns the effective license of the plugin (type, licensee, serial, user limit, expiry dates, source). Jira administrators only.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/license.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestLicense}}; expiry dates are formatted in the caller's locale.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/license.errors: 403 (plain text `permission violation`) for non-administrators; 401 for anonymous callers with `loggedIn=true`.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/licenses.summary: Returns the licenses of the plugin and of every installed companion app (extension) that reports license information. Jira administrators only.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/licenses.response: 200 with a JSON object keyed by app key: `com.almworks.jira.structure` for this plugin, plus each companion app's product key; each value is a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestLicense}}.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects.summary: Lists the projects in which the plugin is enabled and on which the caller has the given project permission, sorted by project name. Optionally attaches project-role information.

params.permission: Jira short permission name; only `browse` (default, browse projects) and `create` (create issues) are accepted. Any other value gives 400.
params.withRoles: Boolean, default false. When true, every project gets `userRoles` and the reply gets `roles`. Note: `userRoles` is the list of ids of all project roles defined in Jira (the same list for every project, not the caller's actual memberships); it is empty for anonymous callers, and `roles` is then omitted.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestProject$Seq}}; each project's `iconUrl` is the small avatar URL.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects.errors: 400 (plain text `invalid permission requested`) for an unsupported permission (Jira's own lookup decides what is supported: it ignores case and accepts key forms such as `BROWSE_PROJECTS` and `createIssue`); 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/roles.summary: Lists all project roles defined in Jira. Logged-in callers only.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/roles.errors: 403 with no body for anonymous callers; 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses.summary: Lists the issue statuses used by the workflows that apply to the given projects and issue types, ordered by status category (to do, in progress, done), each with its category color.

params.projects: Comma-separated project ids, or `*` for all projects that are enabled for the plugin and browsable by the caller (ids outside that set are ignored). Omitted or empty means no projects, so the result is empty.
params.types: Comma-separated issue type ids, or `*` for all types of the selected projects. Omitted or empty means no types (empty result).

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/statuses.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/timezone.summary: Returns a time zone id and its current offset. Without `name` it is the caller's Jira time zone (the default user time zone for anonymous callers).

params.name: Optional time zone id such as `Europe/Berlin`. Unknown ids resolve to `GMT`.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/timezone.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitio.summary: Lists the workflow transitions that lead into the given status in the workflows that apply to the given projects and issue types (transitions whose target is that status; the issue-creation transition is excluded). Each transition names its workflow, action id and source statuses.

params.projects: Comma-separated project ids, or `*` for all projects that are enabled for the plugin and browsable by the caller (ids outside that set are ignored). Omitted or empty means no projects, so the result is empty.
params.types: Comma-separated issue type ids or `*`; omitted or empty means no types (empty result).

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/transitio.errors: 400 (plain text) when `status` is missing (`must have status`) or not a known status (`unknown status`); 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types.summary: Lists the issue types available in the given projects (union over their issue type schemes).

params.projects: Comma-separated project ids, or `*` for all projects that are enabled for the plugin and browsable by the caller (ids outside that set are ignored). Omitted or empty means no projects, so the result is empty.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/types.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui.summary: Computes the configuration of the structure panel embedded in a Jira issue page, project page or agile board: which structure to show initially, the default structure, the caller's panel preferences and whether the caller may change them. The page type is taken from the most specific context given (agile board, else project, else issue). The initial structure is chosen in this order: the only structure visible to the caller (if exactly one), `preferredStructure`, the structure from the navigation hint cookie, then according to the auto-switch mode (structure containing the issue, default structure, or most recently used). Read-only.

params.structure3.navigation.hint: Optional navigation hint cookie set by the client when the user opens an issue from a structure. Format `<structure id>|<anything>|<issue key>`; when its issue key equals the current issue and 'keep structure when navigating' is on (default), that structure is shown initially if the caller can view it.
params.forIssue: Issue id (numeric) of the issue page.
params.forProject: Project key of the project page.
params.forAgileBoard: Agile board id; marks the request as coming from an agile board (an issue in a project where the plugin is disabled is then tolerated).
params.preferredStructure: Structure id to show initially if the caller can view it.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui.errors: 400 (plain text) when no context is given. For `forIssue`: the issue's problem mapped to a status (404 not found or not visible; 500 for an issue with no project, and otherwise), plain text. 404 (plain text) when `forProject` is unknown or not browsable. 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui.summary: Saves the caller's structure-panel preferences (auto-switch mode, auto-collapse, keep structure when navigating) for the project of the given context, then returns the recomputed panel configuration like the GET variant. The auto-switch mode is stored for the issue page when `forIssue` is given, otherwise for the project page. Only keys present in the body are changed; with none present nothing is written. Logged-in callers only.

params.structure3.navigation.hint: Optional navigation hint cookie set by the client when the user opens an issue from a structure. Format `<structure id>|<anything>|<issue key>`; when its issue key equals the current issue and 'keep structure when navigating' is on (default), that structure is shown initially if the caller can view it.
params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestUpdateUIConfigRequest}}: the context (`forIssue`/`forProject`/`forAgileBoard`, at least one) plus any of the preference keys.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui.request: Exactly what the structure panel should show on a Jira page; at least one of `forIssue`, `forProject`, `forAgileBoard` must be given (a positive id or non-empty key). `autoSwitch` must be `off`, `withIssue` or `default`.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/ui.errors: 403 (plain text `permission violation`) for anonymous callers; 400 (plain text) for a missing body, missing context or unknown `autoSwitch` value; issue/project errors as in the GET variant.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/userPicke.summary: Tells whether the caller has Jira's global 'browse users' (user picker) permission.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/userPicke.response: 200 with a bare JSON boolean (`true` or `false`).
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/userPicke.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget.summary: Returns the bootstrap configuration of the structure grid client for the caller: plugin and Jira versions, cluster node, available Jira fields, the caller's capabilities (create issues, bulk change, create/share views, create perspectives, manage global saved columns, admin, anonymous), installed companion-app settings, export menu links, third-party item types, polling back-off, help visibility and a global error notice (shown when Jira's index consistency check failed). Read-only.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget.errors: 403 (plain text `permission violation`) without the plugin's 'use' permission; 500 (plain text) when Jira cannot list the caller's navigable fields.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/is.summary: Returns what happens when the caller clicks an issue link in a structure grid: the caller's own preference if set, else the instance default (Jira application property `structure.board.issueLinkAction`, else the JVM system property of that name, read once at plugin start), else show details.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/is.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/i.summary: Stores the caller's preferred issue-link click action in the caller's Jira user preferences.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget/i.errors: 400 (plain text) for anonymous callers; 400 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} for an unknown `type`; 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta.summary: Returns what the structure dashboard gadget needs to render: the current user, the configured structure, view, canvas-mode view and saved filter (each only if the caller can see it), the Jira issue operations available as links, and any problems found. This resource is not behind the plugin's common access gate; it checks the 'use' permission itself.

params.structureId: Structure id; ignored when absent or not positive. Not viewable or missing: a general error `s.g.no-such-structure` is added.
params.viewId: View id for the normal gadget mode; silently omitted from the reply if missing or not viewable.
params.canvasViewId: View id for the maximized (canvas) gadget mode; same rules as `viewId`.
params.filterId: Jira saved filter id; when not accessible, Jira's error messages are added as general errors.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.javax.GadgetResource$GadgetMeta}}. When the caller lacks the 'use' permission, `errors` holds the general error key `s.g.structure-unavailable` and structure, views and filter are omitted.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/meta.errors: No error statuses of its own; problems are reported inside `errors`.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structure.summary: Structure picker for the gadget configuration form. With a non-blank `query`, searches all structures the caller can view by name (matched text highlighted in the HTML label), returning every match when there are at most 9, else 8 items plus a 'N more' footer. Without a query, suggests up to 8 structures: the caller's recent structures and favorites, balanced 4/4 when both lists are long. This resource is not behind the plugin's common access gate; it checks the 'use' permission itself.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/structure.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestSearchResult}} (one group per category; each item's `entity` is a {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.data.RestStructure}}). When the caller lacks the 'use' permission: 200 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.util.ErrorCollection}} holding the key `s.g.structure-unavailable`.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate.summary: Validates the gadget configuration form. Checks the structure (present and viewable), the view (and the canvas-mode view when canvas settings are used), the filter settings and the row counts (whole numbers 2 to 50). This resource is not behind the plugin's common access gate; it checks the 'use' permission itself.

params.canvas-viewId: View id for canvas mode; checked only when `useCanvasSettings` is true.
params.filterQuery: URL-encoded query text; required for `text`, `jql` (validated as JQL for the caller) and `sjql` (parsed and validated as a structure query).
params.filterId: For `saved`: `filter-<numeric id>` of a Jira saved filter the caller can access.
params.numRows: Number of rows to show, 2 to 50. Required.
params.canvas-numRows: Rows in canvas mode, 2 to 50; checked only when `useCanvasSettings` is true.
params.useCanvasSettings: Boolean, default false: whether separate canvas-mode settings are in use.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/validate.errors: 400 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.util.ErrorCollection}} listing field errors (keyed by the parameter names above). Error texts are message keys (e.g. `s.g.config.err.no.structureId`, `s.g.config.err.bad.numRows` with the bounds as params), except JQL/S-JQL problems which are already-localized messages. Missing 'use' permission is reported as a `structureId` field error.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views.summary: View picker for the gadget configuration form. With a non-empty `query`, searches all views the caller can view by name (every match when there are at most 9, else 8 items plus a 'N more' footer). Otherwise suggests up to 8 views from the menu configured for the given structure (or the global default menu) on the gadget page. This resource is not behind the plugin's common access gate; it checks the 'use' permission itself.

params.structureId: Structure id (text) whose view menu to suggest from; ignored if not viewable.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/views.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestSearchResult}} (each item's `entity` is a {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestView}}). Without the 'use' permission: 200 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.util.ErrorCollection}} holding `s.g.structure-unavailable`.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/gadget/widgetCon.summary: Returns client tuning for the gadget grid in local (same Jira) and remote (gadget shown in another application) modes: poll interval, minimum cached rows and preload factor, plus node-wandering and retry back-off settings for Data Center. Defaults: local 15000 ms / 20 rows / 2.0; remote 15000 ms / 100 rows / 5.0 on Server and 30000 ms / 500 rows / 10.0 on Data Center; each overridable by application or system properties `structure.gadget.<local|remote>.<pollInterval|minCachedRows|preloadRowsFactor>`. No permission check.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.summary: Stores a perspective (a snapshot of the structure page state: structure, view, filters, expansion and so on, as opaque JSON) and returns it with a new id, so it can be shared as a link. The id is a random positive 31-bit integer. Requires a logged-in caller who has the 'use' permission. Stored perspectives are deleted automatically after a period without access.

params.body: {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestPerspective}} without `id`; `spec` is any JSON value (normally an object) describing the page state.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest.v1.data.RestPerspective}} holding the new `id` and the stored `spec` echoed as raw JSON.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.errors: 400 (plain text) for a missing body, a body with an `id`, or an empty `spec`; 401 for anonymous callers (platform default); 403 without the 'use' permission.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.summary: E-mails a link to a stored perspective to Jira users, with an optional personal message (default text when empty). Side effect: if the perspective shows a structure, the caller is an administrator of that structure and has the 'browse users' permission, each recipient who cannot view that structure is granted view access by a new user rule prepended to the structure's permissions. Also counts the share in usage statistics.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.request: `perspectiveId` and a non-empty `recipients` list of Jira user keys are required; every key must resolve to an existing user.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/sha.errors: 400 (plain text) when `perspectiveId` or recipients are missing, an unknown user key is given (message names the key), or Jira outgoing mail is not configured. 404 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the perspective does not exist; 404/403 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}} when the perspective's structure is not viewable by the caller. 401 for anonymous callers.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/{id}.summary: Returns the stored page-state JSON of a perspective. Any caller with the 'use' permission (anonymous included when granted it) can read any perspective by id; there is no owner check. Reading refreshes the perspective's last-used time (protecting it from cleanup) and counts an access and an active user in usage statistics. Saved-column references inside the stored view specifications are refreshed to current definitions before returning.
GET /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/{id}.response: 200 with a JSON string whose content is the perspective's `spec` as JSON text (double-encoded; the client parses it a second time).
GET /rest/structure/1.0/perspective/{id}.errors: 400 (plain text) for an id below 1; 404 (plain text) when no perspective has that id; 403 (plain text) without the 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshoot.summary: Validates the two arguments of the plugin's `structure()` JQL function for the caller without running it: the structure must exist and be viewable, its automation must not be stopped, and the structure query must parse and validate. Logged-in callers only.

params.structure: Structure id or exact structure name (as in the `structure()` JQL function's first argument). Empty gives the `s.jql.error.unknown-structure` error. A name matching several viewable structures is an error.
params.query: Structure query (S-JQL) text, as the function's second argument; missing means `[]`; an empty text is a parse error.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshoot.errors: 400 with a JSON array of message strings (all errors sorted alphabetically, then all warnings sorted). 401 for anonymous callers; 403 (plain text) without the 'use' permission.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshoot.summary: Runs the `structure()` JQL function arguments with maximum logging and streams the captured trace log as a ZIP download (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="S-JQL_Troubleshooting.zip"`) containing one entry `S-JQL_Troubleshooting.log`. While it runs, trace logging of the plugin's query subsystem is captured into the archive; if the arguments are invalid nothing is executed and the log entry stays empty (the messages go to the server log instead). Logged-in callers only; no administrator check. Writes start/finish warnings to the server log.

params.structure: Structure id or exact structure name (as in the `structure()` JQL function's first argument). Empty gives the `s.jql.error.unknown-structure` error. A name matching several viewable structures is an error.
params.query: Structure query (S-JQL) text, as the function's second argument; missing means `[]`; an empty text is a parse error.
params.includeRelOutput: Boolean, default false: also capture the step-by-step relation evaluation output (very verbose).
params.messagePattern: Optional log line layout pattern (log4j pattern syntax) for the captured lines; default layout when omitted.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshoot.errors: 401 for anonymous callers; 403 (plain text) without the 'use' permission. Argument errors do not change the status.

PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/dismi.summary: Records that the calling administrator declined the offer to send anonymous usage statistics to the vendor, so the offer is no longer shown to them. Jira administrators only.

PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enabl.summary: Records the administrator's consent to send usage statistics (the original then sends them, with the Jira server id, to its vendor every day). The replacement stores the setting and never uploads anything (section 1.8). Jira administrators only.

POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/reco.summary: Adds client-side usage counters to the plugin's local usage statistics for the given time: each entry of `stats` is added as a total count, the caller is counted as a unique user, and also as an active user if any key is one of the interactive actions (e.g. `expandAll`, `view.switch`, `layout.switch`, `search.toggle`). Any counter name is accepted except those that collide with the entries the call adds itself (`userCount`, or `activeUser` together with an interactive action): those give 400 `Invalid request data` and record nothing. Silently does nothing for anonymous callers or when `stats` is empty or `timestamp` is missing.
POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/reco.errors: 403 (plain text) when the caller lacks the plugin's 'use' permission (enforced by the common access gate, see conventions); 401 when the query string carries `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous.

GET /rest/structure/1.0/view.summary: Searches views (saved grid column layouts) the caller can access at the requested level, optionally restricted to given ids and/or a name pattern.

params.ids: Comma-separated view ids; non-numeric or non-positive entries are skipped; ids the caller cannot access are silently left out.
params.name: Name search text: a case-insensitive literal substring anywhere in the name (`ann` matches `Planning`); ignored if it contains nothing searchable.
params.permission: Minimum permission level the caller must have on each view, case-insensitive: `none`, `view`, `edit`, `automate`, `admin` (`edit_generators` is a deprecated alias). Levels at or below `view` mean `view`. Default `view`.
params.withPermissions: Boolean, default false: include each view's permission rules (only for views the caller administers).
params.withOwner: Boolean, default false: include the owner as a user object when the caller is the owner, a Jira administrator or has 'browse users'; otherwise only `hasOwner` is set.

POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta.summary: Validates a predictive-CFD gadget configuration and returns what the gadget needs to render: the current user and the scope and training structures (if viewable by the caller). When the feature is disabled, only a general error is returned. The predictive cumulative-flow (CFD) feature can be switched off by the system property `structure.pcfd.enabled=false` (on by default). These endpoints are not behind the plugin's common access gate.
POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta.request: Checks: both structures viewable; `trainingPeriod` one of -1, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 56; `teamAttributeSpec` and `whenCompletedAttributeSpec` present; `targetDate` (if given) in `YYYY-MM-DD` form; `ignoreThreshold` (if given) 0 to 100; `estimationIssueTypes` and `scopeIssueTypes` non-empty lists of existing issue type ids that do not overlap. `adjustments` is not checked.
POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.cfd.rest.data.RestCfdGadgetMetaResponse}}; problems are listed in `errors` as field errors keyed by the request key (localized messages), the reply status stays 200.
POST /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/meta.errors: None of its own; a malformed JSON body is not translated by the plugin and gets the platform's generic error reply.

GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/status.summary: Tells whether the predictive-CFD feature is enabled on this instance. The predictive cumulative-flow (CFD) feature can be switched off by the system property `structure.pcfd.enabled=false` (on by default). These endpoints are not behind the plugin's common access gate.

GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate.summary: Same validation as the POST meta call, taking the settings as query parameters, and answering only with the errors. The predictive cumulative-flow (CFD) feature can be switched off by the system property `structure.pcfd.enabled=false` (on by default). These endpoints are not behind the plugin's common access gate.

params.scopeStructureId: Structure id holding the work to forecast.
params.trainingStructureId: Structure id holding historical work used to learn throughput.
params.trainingPeriod: History window in days: 7, 14, 21, 28, 42 or 56, or -1 for all history.
params.estimationIssueTypes: Repeatable; issue type ids of the container items (e.g. epics) whose size is estimated from history.
params.scopeIssueTypes: Repeatable; issue type ids of the work items (e.g. stories) that are counted.
params.teamAttributeSpec: JSON text of an attribute spec giving each item's team; unparseable JSON counts as absent.
params.whenAppearedAttributeSpec: JSON attribute spec giving when an item appeared.
params.whenWorkStartedAttributeSpec: JSON attribute spec giving when work on an item started.
params.whenCompletedAttributeSpec: JSON attribute spec giving when an item was completed. Required.

GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate.response: 200 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestEmpty}} when valid. When the feature is disabled the reply is 400 with the 'not enabled' general error.
GET /rest/cfd/1.0/gadget/validate.errors: 400 with {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.util.ErrorCollection}} (localized messages, field errors keyed by parameter name).

POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd.summary: Runs a Monte Carlo forecast of when the work in the scope structure will be finished, per team and overall, and returns the cumulative-flow chart (past plus simulated future) and per-team statistics. Throughput per team is learned from items completed in the training structure within the training period; containers without enough child items get extra predicted items based on the historical average per container. Per-team percentage adjustments and an ignore threshold (teams whose share of the total item count is at most that percentage are not simulated and are lumped together as `Other` when there are several) shape the result. Items without a team value belong to team `No Team`. The reply includes a human-readable calculation trace unless the system property `structure.cfd.disableTracing` is on. Read-only; dates use the caller's Jira time zone. The predictive cumulative-flow (CFD) feature can be switched off by the system property `structure.pcfd.enabled=false` (on by default). These endpoints are not behind the plugin's common access gate.
POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd.request: `scopeStructureId`, `trainingStructureId` and `config` (with both issue type lists) are required. `simulations` defaults to 50 runs. The `config` must also give all four attribute specs (`teamAttributeSpec`, `whenAppearedAttributeSpec`, `whenWorkStartedAttributeSpec`, `whenCompletedAttributeSpec`), each with an id and a standard format; otherwise the run fails with the generic error below. (The meta and validate calls check only the team and completed specs.)
POST /rest/cfd/1.0/simulation/cfd.errors: Missing required input or a disabled feature raise errors that this module does not translate (no plugin exception mapper is installed for it): expect the platform's generic error response, normally status 500. With the feature disabled the original builds a 403 reply but throws it in a way no mapper handles, so the caller still gets the generic error. A `targetDate` not in `YYYY-MM-DD` form fails the same way.

conventions:
#### Authentication and access
- Paths: module `rest-v1` is served under `/rest/structure/1.0`, module `rest-cfd` under `/rest/cfd/1.0` (Jira 9.x).
- Authentication is Jira's usual (session cookie, basic auth, tokens). An endpoint without an anonymous marker requires a logged-in user; anonymous calls get 401 from the platform. Endpoints marked anonymous-allowed carry both platform annotations for anonymous access (classic anonymous access and anonymous site access), so they also answer anonymous callers; what an anonymous caller then sees depends on the plugin's own checks.
- Common access gate (all `rest-v1` and `rest-v2` resources except the gadget resource `/gadget/*`; not applied to `rest-cfd`). Before the method runs: (1) if the query string has `loggedIn=true` and the caller is anonymous, the reply is 401 with no body; (2) if the method or its resource is marked administrator-only, the caller must be a Jira administrator (or system administrator where so marked), else 403 with plain-text body `permission violation`; (3) otherwise the caller must hold the plugin's 'use' application permission (configured by the Jira admin; may be granted to anonymous users), else 403 `permission violation`, unless the method is explicitly exempt.
- Administrator-only endpoints in these modules: in `rest-v1`, `GET /config/license`, `GET /config/licenses`, `PUT /statistics/enableSending`, `PUT /statistics/dismissOffer`; in `rest-v2`, the whole `/attribute-sensitivity`, `/configuration` and `/dark-features` resources, and the whole `/cloudmigration` resource for system administrators only. None of them requires websudo; the only websudo-protected resource of the plugin is the dark-features resource of `rest-v2`.
- XSRF: the platform's standard protection applies to mutating methods (POST, PUT, DELETE): requests with form or plain-text content types are rejected unless they carry `X-Atlassian-Token: no-check`; JSON requests pass. No endpoint opts out. Some POSTs take a dummy JSON body only to force a JSON content type.
- No CORS opt-in.

#### Error responses
Errors come in two body formats:
- Plain text (`Content-Type: text/plain`): the message(s), several joined by newlines, or an empty body. Used for most explicit validation failures (400), permission failures (403 `permission violation`), not-found (404), and server errors (500, body = exception message).
- Structured error object, {{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestStructureError}}, as JSON, for errors raised by the plugin's domain layer.

For `rest-v1` (and `rest-v2`) an exception mapper translates uncaught exceptions:
- unparseable request JSON: 400, error object with `error` = `Cannot parse request JSON` plus the parser's message;
- plugin stopped or a background job failure: 503, plain text `service unavailable`;
- an explicit 'error response' raised by the code: exactly that response (status, headers, body);
- invalid input (illegal argument, invalid data): 400, error object with `error` = `Invalid request data` and `message`;
- forest lock timeout: 500, plain text;
- a domain error: error object with `code`, `error` (the error name with its code, as `<NAME>[<code>]`, for example `INVALID_JQL[6003]`), `message`, `localizedMessage` `rowId` (0 when no row is concerned) and, when known, `structureId`, `viewId`, `itemId`, `itemDescription`; status from the error's category: not found 404, no permission 403, invalid input 400, anything else 500;
- anything else: 500, plain text with the exception message (and an error in the server log).

Note that the plugin reports 'does not exist' and 'not visible to you' with the same 404 so as not to reveal existence.

#### The plugin's own error codes
Besides the public codes of `StructureErrors` (Part 2, `API.md`), the plugin raises its own domain errors with codes 6000–6099. Their `code`, `error` (name) and category are part of the contract: they reach clients in the structure-error object above and Java callers through `StructureException`. The table gives the name; on the wire `error` carries the code as well, as `<name>[<code>]` (for example `INVALID_JQL[6003]`).

| code | `error` | category | raised when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6001 | `JIRA_DATA_ACCESS_EXCEPTION` | `INTERNAL` | reading Jira data failed |
| 6002 | `SEARCH_ERROR` | `INTERNAL` | a Jira search failed |
| 6003 | `INVALID_JQL` | `INVALID_INPUT` | a JQL text does not parse or validate |
| 6004 | `INACCESSIBLE_FILTER` | `NOT_FOUND` | a saved filter does not exist or the user may not see it |
| 6005 | `INVALID_SJQL` | `INVALID_INPUT` | an S-JQL (structure query) text does not parse or validate |
| 6006 | `PERMISSION_RULE_APPLICATION_FORMS_CYCLE` | `INVALID_INPUT` | structure permission rules that apply other structures' rules form a cycle |
| 6007 | `APPLY_RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE` | `INVALID_INPUT` | a permission rule applies a structure whose rules cannot be applied |
| 6008 | `ACTING_USER_NOT_FOUND` | `NO_PERMISSION` | the user a forest source or job should act as no longer exists |
| 6009 | `CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_MODULE` | `GENERAL` | an extension module does not support the requested operation |
| 6010 | `GROUP_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` | `NOT_FOUND` | a group named in permission rules does not exist |
| 6011 | `PROJECT_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` | `NOT_FOUND` | a project named in permission rules does not exist |
| 6012 | `PROJECT_ROLE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` | `NOT_FOUND` | a project role named in permission rules does not exist |
| 6013 | `USER_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESIBLE` | `NOT_FOUND` | a user named in permission rules does not exist (the name is spelled this way, with one S in INACCESIBLE) |
| 6014 | `CONCURRENT_UPDATE_FAILED` | `INTERNAL` | a change could not be saved after repeated concurrent changes |
| 6015 | `INVALID_EXPR` | `INVALID_INPUT` | a formula (expression) does not parse or validate |
| 6016 | `ATTRIBUTE_LOADER_PROBLEM` | `INTERNAL` | an attribute could not be loaded |
| 6017 | `ENTITY_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` | `NOT_FOUND` | an object that is neither a structure, view nor item (for example an effector process) does not exist or the user may not see it |

`rest-cfd` has no such mapper: its failures surface as the platform's generic error reply (normally 500).

#### Caching and other headers
- Responses carry `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store` unless the endpoint itself set `Cache-Control` or an `ETag` (applies to all gated resources and the gadget resource; `rest-cfd` sets it only on its validate call).
- On Data Center, the polling and attribute-subscription resources of `rest-v2` add a cookie `X-Structure-DC-Meta` = URL-encoded `<node id>|<retry count>` (retry count = live nodes times a multiplier, at least 1), unless switched off by the system property `structure.dcRestInterceptor.disabled`.

#### Rate limiting
Only the structure search endpoints of `rest-v2` are rate limited: one request per user per configured interval (anonymous callers share one bucket); a faster request gets 429 with `Retry-After: <seconds>` and a localized plain-text message. Nothing in `rest-v1` or `rest-cfd` is rate limited.

#### Content types and conventions
- Requests and responses are JSON (`application/json`, UTF-8) unless stated; the gadget resource also accepts form-encoded requests; the S-JQL logs endpoint streams `application/zip`.
- Many replies use the acknowledgement object `{"empty": true}` ({{com.almworks.structure.commons.rest.RestEmpty}}) instead of an empty body.
- Optional values are usually omitted or null when not applicable; clients must treat absent and null alike.
- Ids: structure, view, row, issue and project ids are JSON integers; Jira issue type, status and constant ids are strings. Times are epoch milliseconds unless stated.
- Long-running `rest-v2` requests use the asynchronous job protocol described with {{com.almworks.jira.structure.rest2g.data.RestExtensibleRequest}}.
